newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy presses for new Albanian government soon.
newsitem.headline: Italy presses for new Albanian government soon.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha told Italy on Tuesday that a new national unity government would be formed within 24 hours as Rome pressed for swift action on a political solution to spreading unrest in the Balkan state.
A Foreign Ministry official said Berisha had advised Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini in a telephone call that the new government "will be established within 24 hours".

Dini, who is spearheading international efforts to help resolve the Albanian crisis, urged Berisha to ensure that the new cabinet was drawn from a broad range of political parties and from various regions, the official said.

He spoke shortly before Albanian television said Berisha had appointed Bashkim Fino, an economist from the southern town of Gjirokaster and a member of the main opposition Socialist Party, as new prime minister.

Fino replaces Aleksander Meksi, a member of the ruling Democratic Party, who resigned last month as unrest unleashed by popular anger over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes mushroomed into an armed uprising in several southern towns.

Italy on Monday brokered a deal in which rebel leaders from the southern port Vlore agreed to end their uprising in return for swift implementation of a peace deal between Berisha and his political opponents.
On Sunday Albania asked Italy to underwrite the agreement, which envisages a national unity government, early elections by June and an amnesty for rebels who lay down their arms.
Dini on Monday cancelled a trip planned for this week to India so that he could follow the Albanian crisis, the Italian Foreign Ministry said.
Italy, which briefly occupied Albania under Fascism in World War Two, has strong cultural and commercial links with the tiny Balkan state, Europe's poorest country.
It has been active in seeking a peaceful end to the unrest and has bolstered its military presence in the Adriatic out of fear that all-out war could trigger an exodus of refugees.
Italy has evacuated 78 foreigners from Vlore in the past week in three rescue missions using military helicopters.
The Foreign Ministry on Tuesday repeated advice to Italians not to travel to Albania unless absolutely necessary and to those living there to remain in close touch with their embassy in Tirana.
It noted that contingency plans had been drawn up for some time to evacuate Italians if necessary.
